Ignatiev is (or at least was as he may have revised his views to some extent by now) a particularly radical Jewish Communist (he was involved in forming some dissident faction from the Communist Party USA after that group broke from Stalinism after Khrushchev's secret speech) that like his equally radical and non-Jewish cohort Theodore Allen thinks whiteness as a social category and basis of identity is a source of oppression. Hence he advocates abolishing the concept of the white race with whites instead embracing a broader humanism in the cause of fighting oppression. Contrary to some alarmist views Ignatiev doesn't advocate genocide against whites though his views, in their implications, would tend to undermine whites in any moral claims to maintain themselves demographically.

In his views of white identity he is similar to New Left icon Tom Hayden. Hayden believed Irish-Americans like himself should reject the oppressive social category of whiteness in favor of Irish identity as he believed the history of being oppressed gave the Irish much grounding to identify with colored peoples.

More generally this stuff is an offshoot of Max Horkheimer's critical theory in applying his techniques specifically to race; or critical race theory, to be specific.
